/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
An 18-year-old man is referred to a psychiatrist for evaluation after a recent suicide attempt. On questioning him, he says that he did it because he got fed up with life and feels that he is worthless. The patient’s father informs the doctor that his son has been gloomy most of the time over the last 2 months, and his academic performance has declined significantly. His father further adds that his son’s appetite has decreased significantly over the last 3 months, leading to a 5.0 kg (11.0 lb) weight loss.  The patient denies any history of manic or hypomanic episodes. Physical examination is unremarkable. Routine laboratory tests, including thyroid hormone and cortisol levels, are within normal limits. Which of the following patterns of abnormal brain activity would most likely be present in this patient?

Options:
A. Increased serotonergic activity in frontal cortex
B. Increased dopaminergic activity in the limbic system
C. Increased glutamatergic activity in the subthalamic nucleus
D. Decreased norepinephrine levels in the cortical and limbic areas
E. Decreased cholinergic activity in the hippocampus and amygdala

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns depressive symptomatology and the neurobiological correlates of major depressive disorder, which falls within psychiatry and mental health."}
